register: # SOURCE: ABB/Power-One 'ABB SunSpec Inverter Modbus Map' workbook (J. Blair, 2013; sheets 'Inverter Modbus' and 'Status and Events'), a vendor document. Offsets are the workbook's absolute 0-based register addresses, which are the on-wire addresses (base 0, SunSpec marker 'SunS' at registers 0-1).

# APPLIES TO: legacy ABB/Power-One inverters with native SunSpec Modbus (PVI 10/12K, TRIO, Central, Ultra). It does NOT apply to a VSN300/VSN700 datalogger or to a REACT2: a logger serves models 1, 103, 160 and then 120/121/123, so it matches this map only up to register 171 and registers 172+ (vendor model 64061 here) would return unrelated data.

# SCALING: ABB fixes the SunSpec scale factors in this document (A_SF=-2, V_SF=-2, W_SF=0, Hz_SF=-2, WH_SF=0, Tmp_SF=-1; model 160 DCA_SF=DCV_SF=-1) so fixed unit multipliers are used. Points ABB marks as unimplemented (constant 0x8000/0xFFFF) are left out: line voltages AB/BC/CA, VA, VAr, PF, DCA, DCV, heat-sink and transformer temperature, and model 160 DCW/DCWH/Tmp.

# BYTE ORDER: SunSpec big-endian, high register first (the app default), for 32-bit integers and float32 alike; no Register_Endian adjustment needed. Energy counters in model 64061 have no unit in the vendor table; Wh is assumed (the Aurora counters are watt-hours).

# NOT COVERED: control block 143-173 (writable power limits and ramps); TRIO-only blocks 64062 (comm board, 298), model 403 string combiners (336 and 394; their scale factors are not fixed, so they need a dynamic scale-factor adjustment) and 64063 (fuse board, 452); Alarm4-Alarm8 (unused in practice). Serial parameters are not stated in this workbook; the Modbus slave id is the inverter address (register 68).

note: ABB uses 66 registers (the SunSpec standard is 65), so the next model starts at 70
